transcript.text: I'll tell you a very sad story. I got to
the point where my gym was packed. Like
I had two sessions running at any given
time. I had a strength session and a
cardio session, 40-50 people, and I only
had 3,500 sq ft of actual like gym
space. What's crazy is that because I
couldn't fit any more people in, what I
decided to do was I decided to cut the
session times in half. And what happened
next was I churned out like a third of
my customer base cuz they were like,
"Why'd you change it? It was so great."
What I should have done was say, "Oh, I
nailed it. I should open another
location." Now, if I wasn't making
enough profit, then I should have fixed
my price. Like if you finally figure out
what actually like what people love,
that is the hardest thing to do. And so
once they love it, if your business
model is profitable, don't mess with it.
Just do more. Go open up more locations.
If people love it and it's not
profitable, then fix your pricing.
